scope: Synthetic text fixture and deterministic client of existing private provider/tool. Not a model benchmark or production qualification.

questions.failure: index-only recovery method lost correction links

acceptance: Preserve and hash every synthetic original, including the exact copy and conflicting publication.
Exact copies share content identity and do not create additional claim records; different hashes do not prove independence.
The corrected lookup retains version 1 and its withdrawal record while returning version 2.
Do not produce a configuration from ambiguity, absence, withdrawn evidence or invalid evidence.
Returned passages must occur in originals with matching hashes; this is not a general entailment test.
Configuration values must be independently checked against this frozen rubric.
Compare raw lexical retrieval and the same retrieval with supplied lifecycle/dedup metadata; disclose annotation costs and refrain from model-quality claims.
Restore sources, annotations, claims, corrections, runtime code and client from a pinned archive into a fresh target and execute every case again.
Make original generated data location unavailable during replay; deny Python reads outside restored data and declared runtime, and deny socket access in replay processes.
Compare fresh restored outputs by statuses, claims, snapshots and evidence identities, excluding only timestamps and relocated absolute paths.
Obtain separate review of the exact code and report before describing the demonstration as reviewed.
